admission: A newer motivating service invokes a typed callback with a declared first-party generated HTTP wrapper, escaping the previously released direct native-client proof.
policy: Require an explicit ABC or Protocol for a service operation that awaits a typed callback using a source-proven active native HTTP wrapper. Preserve contract ancestry, value and lifecycle exclusions, unresolved ownership and escape guards.

selection.description: Complete package Python in the candidate; complete tracked Python in one immutable private consumer; the same fixed public-source sample as SQL calibration; generic isolated namespace/distribution projects and two linked-source reproductions.
selection.private_pins: Full source, project and lock input closures retained privately; no private source, locations or identifying pins exported.

method.baseline: Released 1.76.0 detector in the current engine with only its legacy diagnostic message header normalized.
method.timing_context: Median of three per-corpus trial totals, summing isolated batch analysis times for each temperature. Worker startup is excluded. Rule-focused measurements on the shared VM do not establish full-engine fleet overhead.

review.method: Every newly added consumer diagnostic was independently inspected; unchanged findings were reconciled by complete diagnostic tuples. Private audit details remain in separate receipts.
review.independent_semantic_reviews: Generated-client ownership, eager resource lifecycle, decorator and mutation guards, nominal source-cache isolation and baseline compatibility were reviewed independently. The finite labels and inspected findings do not establish universal precision or recall.

compatibility: Restoring the legacy SARJ465 message anchor retains all 24 preexisting consumer baseline identities without growing diagnostic baselines or withdrawing expanded service detection.
limits: Proof is deliberately bounded to stable declared first-party HTTP wrappers and a single typed callback argument; opaque, mutated, decorated or escaping ownership abstains.
Generated providers are admitted for HTTP and SQL ownership proof; nominal-ID source inventory keeps its previous generated-source exclusion.
The original two campaigns of 100 distinct cases remain separate historical evidence; these 44 cases are additional semantic controls, not repeated claims of new hundred-pass audits.
Canonical repository verification and latest exact-head hosted CI remain separate merge gates.
